findings.reason: the endpoint needs the decrease restricted to families whose divergence the sources do not explain (or the recorded reason accepted in place of the decrease), or a node that finds the audit green and the count unchanged has no authorised way to close.
findings.text: §5's done-when requires the domain audit to report zero names whose stored domain disagrees with the stored decision AND the census's grouping axis to count strictly fewer multi-domain families; `physics_domain` is derived from DD sources (`sn-catalog-grouping` §3: `select_primary_domain` over `source_domains`), and §5's own prose allows a family to remain multi-domain when its members "draw on DD sources whose domains differ" — so once the audit is green a legitimately multi-domain family is counted at both ends, and the only way to move the count is to write a domain the derivation contradicts, which fails the same done-when's first clause

findings.reason: as written a node must either invent a second reading the plan does not name or drop the population restriction, and the restriction is exactly what stops the full-DD continuation's new names from moving the comparison, so losing it reinstates the defect an earlier review closed.
findings.text: the count is declared "over the families and member names live when this section starts" but pinned to "the consistency census's grouping axis", and the committed census emits per-family `domain_variants` aggregated over all live members plus a bare member-id list (`sib-consistency-census.json`), with no per-member domain and no population argument — and §2 line 46 records that the census has "no way to scope it to a population" and that a population argument only "may be added", so the scoped figure has no sanctioned instrument behind it and §5 does not depend on §2
